category_title: English-dominant Chinese immigrant students with ADHD and Chinese language learning difficulties
minimal_context: Eric is in an individual lesson working on a worksheet where he needs to use Chinese words to make sentences in writing.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Eric, it is time for your individual lesson. Please look at this worksheet and use these Chinese words to make sentences in writing.

STUDENT: (Moves about in his seat and begins biting his finger while looking at the Chinese words.)

TUTOR: You need to focus on your worksheet so that you can progress at the same pace as your peers.

STUDENT: (Continues moving about anxiously and bites his finger harder, looking increasingly agitated.)

TUTOR: I am reminding you again that you need to focus. We have to cover the same amount of content as the rest of the class.

STUDENT: (Pulls his hair and screams in frustration.)

options.A: Constantly probe Eric with questions about the Chinese words to check for his understanding.
options.B: Agree with Eric that he is having a rough time with the Chinese sentence worksheet.
options.C: Tell Eric that if he sees himself getting angry, he should walk out for water.
options.D: Guide Eric to complete the worksheet using the Chinese words to make sentences in writing.
